nodes.title: the Mornyuk signature
nodes.statement: The Mornyuk system concerns objects called reldjens. There are exactly 4 of them: nakopal, kagel, korrreld, iskbra. Two operations are written <> and #. One relation is written ::, read as "yields to".

nodes.title: the Mornyuk combination tables
nodes.statement: The value of x <> y for every pair of reldjens is fixed by the table of the first operation, and likewise for #. The pairs standing in the :: relation are listed in full.

nodes.title: closure under the first operation
nodes.statement: For all reldjens x and y, x <> y is again a reldjen.

nodes.title: association of the first operation
nodes.statement: For all reldjens x, y, z: (x <> y) <> z = x <> (y <> z).

nodes.title: commutation of the first operation
nodes.statement: For all reldjens x and y: x <> y = y <> x.

nodes.title: a neutral object for the first operation
nodes.statement: There is a reldjen kagel with kagel <> x = x <> kagel = x for every x.

nodes.title: an absorbing object for the first operation
nodes.statement: There is a reldjen nakopal with nakopal <> x = x <> nakopal = nakopal for every x.

nodes.title: closure under the second operation
nodes.statement: For all reldjens x and y, x # y is again a reldjen.

nodes.title: association of the second operation
nodes.statement: For all reldjens x, y, z: (x # y) # z = x # (y # z).

nodes.title: commutation of the second operation
nodes.statement: For all reldjens x and y: x # y = y # x.

nodes.title: a neutral object for the second operation
nodes.statement: There is a reldjen nakopal with nakopal # x = x for every x.

nodes.title: reflexivity of the relation
nodes.statement: For every reldjen x: x :: x.

nodes.title: antisymmetry of the relation
nodes.statement: For all reldjens x and y: if x :: y and y :: x then x = y.

nodes.title: transitivity of the relation
nodes.statement: For all reldjens x, y, z: if x :: y and y :: z then x :: z.

nodes.title: comparability of every pair
nodes.statement: For all reldjens x and y, at least one of x :: y and y :: x holds.

nodes.title: the system does not have reversal under the first operation
nodes.statement: Some reldjen x admits no reldjen y for which x <> y and y <> x both land on a neutral object.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = nakopal, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the system does not have self combination under the first operation
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For every reldjen x: x <> x = x.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = korrreld, value = nakopal, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the system does not have cancellation in the first operation
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For all reldjens x, y, z: if x <> y = x <> z then y = z.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = nakopal, y = nakopal, z = kagel, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the system does not have self combination under the second operation
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For every reldjen x: x # x = x.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = kagel, value = korrreld, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the system does not have spreading of the second operation over the first
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For all reldjens x, y, z: x # (y <> z) = (x # y) <> (x # z), and the same on the right.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = kagel, y = nakopal, z = kagel, left = kagel, right = korrreld, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the system does not have the absorption pair
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For all reldjens x and y: x <> (x # y) = x and x # (x <> y) = x.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = kagel, y = kagel, value = korrreld, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the system does not have agreement of the relation with the first operation
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For all reldjens x, y, z: if x :: y then (z <> x) :: (z <> y) and (x <> z) :: (y <> z).

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = kagel, y = korrreld, z = korrreld, side = left, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the system does not have agreement of the relation with the second operation
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For all reldjens x, y, z: if x :: y then (z # x) :: (z # y) and (x # z) :: (y # z).

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = nakopal, y = kagel, z = iskbra, side = left, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: duthnyr reldjens
nodes.statement: A reldjen x is called duthnyr when x <> x = x.

nodes.title: reldjens that korrfex
nodes.statement: Two reldjens x and y are said to korrfex when x <> y = y <> x.

nodes.title: zammorn collections
nodes.statement: A collection S of reldjens is zammorn when x <> y belongs to S for every pair x, y drawn from S.

nodes.title: the drivor of a reldjen
nodes.statement: The drivor of a reldjen x is the collection of reldjens y for which x :: y holds.

nodes.title: the lornumb
nodes.statement: The reldjen kagel is called the lornumb of the system. It is the unique reldjen that leaves every reldjen unchanged under <>.

nodes.title: the vashreld
nodes.statement: The vashreld of the system is the collection of reldjens that korrfex with every reldjen.

nodes.title: the umbka
nodes.statement: The umbka is the collection of all duthnyr reldjens.

nodes.title: the nakgrix of a reldjen
nodes.statement: The nakgrix of a reldjen x, written [x], is the smallest zammorn collection that contains x.

nodes.title: a thrapyr
nodes.statement: A reldjen f is a thrapyr when f :: y holds for every reldjen y, that is, when the drivor of f is the whole system.

nodes.title: driumb reldjens
nodes.statement: A reldjen x is driumb when x <> x equals the lornumb.

nodes.title: the solglim of a reldjen
nodes.statement: The solglim of a reldjen x is the number of reldjens in its nakgrix [x].

nodes.title: the ponshen
nodes.statement: The ponshen of the system is the collection of reldjens whose solglim is largest.

nodes.title: korrjen pairs
nodes.statement: Two distinct reldjens x and y form a korrjen pair when x :: y and y :: x both hold, that is, when each lies in the drivor of the other.

nodes.title: the lornumb is the only one of its kind
nodes.statement: There is exactly one reldjen e with e <> x = x <> e = x for every reldjen x.

verification.domain: every object paired with every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Suppose e and f both leave every reldjen unchanged.
Then e <> f = f, reading e as neutral on the left.
And e <> f = e, reading f as neutral on the right.
So e = f, and the two suppositions describe the same object.

nodes.title: the lornumb lies in the vashreld
nodes.statement: The lornumb korrfexs with every reldjen.

verification.domain: the anchor against every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let e be the lornumb and x any reldjen.
Then e <> x = x and x <> e = x.
So e <> x = x <> e, which is what it means to korrfex.
Since x was arbitrary, e belongs to the vashreld.

nodes.title: the vashreld is zammorn
nodes.statement: If x and y both korrfex with every reldjen, then so does x <> y.

verification.domain: every ordered pair drawn from the core
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let x and y lie in the vashreld and let z be any reldjen.
Then (x <> y) <> z = x <> (y <> z).
Move z past y, then past x, using that each korrfexs with everything.
So x <> y korrfexs with z, and the vashreld is zammorn.

nodes.title: the nakgrix of a reldjen is zammorn
nodes.statement: For every reldjen x, the collection [x] is zammorn.

verification.domain: every object, then every pair inside its span
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: [x] is built by taking x and closing under <>.
Closing under an operation is exactly the sealing condition.
The carrier is finite, so the closure stops after finitely many rounds.

nodes.title: the nakgrix is contained in every zammorn collection
nodes.statement: If S is zammorn and contains x, then S contains all of [x].

verification.domain: every sealed collection against every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Every member of [x] is reached from x by finitely many applications of the operation.
A sealed S containing x is closed under each of those applications.
So each member of [x] is in S, by induction on the number of applications.

nodes.title: a reldjen is duthnyr exactly when its solglim is one
nodes.statement: x <> x = x holds if and only if [x] contains x alone.

verification.domain: every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: If x <> x = x then {x} is already closed under <>.
So [x] = {x} and the solglim is one.
Conversely a span of one object must contain x <> x, which is then x.

nodes.title: the solglim divides the number of reldjens
nodes.statement: For every reldjen x, the solglim of x divides 4.

verification.domain: every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: [x] is a zammorn collection.
Its size is the solglim of x.
The claim is that this size always divides 4.

nodes.title: the nakgrix of a vashreld reldjen stays in the vashreld
nodes.statement: If x lies in the vashreld then every reldjen of [x] lies in the vashreld.

verification.domain: every object of the core, then its span
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: The vashreld is zammorn.
[x] is the smallest zammorn collection containing x.
A smallest such collection sits inside any other, and the vashreld is one.

nodes.title: the umbka is zammorn
nodes.statement: If x and y are both duthnyr then so is x <> y.

verification.domain: every ordered pair drawn from the ridge
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let x and y be duthnyr.
The claim asks whether (x <> y) <> (x <> y) returns x <> y.
Whether it does is settled by running the operation table on every such pair.

nodes.title: drivors are nested along the relation
nodes.statement: If y lies in the drivor of x, then the drivor of y is contained in the drivor of x.

verification.domain: every ordered triple
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let y satisfy x :: y and let z satisfy y :: z.
Transitivity gives x :: z.
So every member of the drivor of y is a member of that of x.

nodes.title: there is at most one thrapyr
nodes.statement: No two distinct reldjens can both be thrapyrs.

verification.domain: every candidate against every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let f and h both be floors.
Then f :: h, since h is any object, and h :: f likewise.
Antisymmetry forces f = h.

nodes.title: the system has a thrapyr
nodes.statement: Some reldjen thrapyrs the whole system.

verification.domain: every candidate against every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Every pair is comparable, so the relation orders the objects into a line.
The claim is that the line has a bottom.
The carrier is finite, so the search over candidates terminates.

nodes.title: no korrjen pairs exist
nodes.statement: No two distinct reldjens lie in each other's drivor.

verification.domain: every ordered pair
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Suppose x and y form a tight pair.
Antisymmetry then identifies x with y.
So a tight pair of distinct objects cannot arise.

nodes.title: every reldjen lies in the vashreld
nodes.statement: Every pair of reldjens korrfexs.

verification.domain: every ordered pair
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: The vashreld is defined by korrfexing with everything.
The claim is that x <> y = y <> x for every pair.
That is settled by scanning the table for a pair that disagrees.

nodes.title: where every reldjen is duthnyr breaks down
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: x <> x = x for every reldjen x.

verification.domain: every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = korrreld, value = nakopal, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: where some reldjen reaches every other breaks down
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: There is a reldjen whose nakgrix is the whole system.

verification.domain: every object and its span
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case largest_span = 2, size = 4, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: where the relation reads the same in both directions breaks down
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: If x :: y then y :: x.

verification.domain: every ordered pair
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = nakopal, y = kagel, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: where the lornumb swallows everything breaks down
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: e <> x equals the lornumb for every reldjen x.

verification.domain: the anchor against every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case anchor = kagel, x = nakopal, value = nakopal, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the second operation keeps the vashreld intact
nodes.statement: If x and y lie in the vashreld then so does x # y.

verification.domain: every ordered pair from the core
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: The vashreld is already zammorn under <>.
The second operation is defined on every pair.
The claim is that # respects the vashreld as well.
